title: Normalize OpenAI-style tool invocation payloads and stabilize streaming tool-message framing
author: Maya Patel
commits_summary: 4 commits: 1) add canonical ToolPayload and mapper with permissive input parsing; 2) stabilize streaming framer to coalesce fragmented tool messages and attach schema tags; 3) SDK helpers + tests for tool_choice semantics; 4) docs and changelog updates + final artifacts
description:
Motivation: different OpenAI-style models emit function/tool calling payloads with small shape and framing variations (partial JSON fragments in streaming, tool messages using either 'tool' or 'name', tool_choice semantics unclear when multiple tools are suggested). This PR adds a thin normalization layer in the OpenAI compatibility path that canonicalizes incoming tool invocation messages into a single ToolPayload shape and fixes streaming fragmentation so tool messages are emitted atomically to callers.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduce pkg/api/openai_compat/normalize.go: permissive mapper that accepts common variants ("tool" vs "name", nested "arguments" vs flat, content-type tags) and emits a canonical ToolPayload. The mapper records source-variant metadata for observability and fallback heuristics.
- Streaming framer changes in pkg/streaming/framer.go: coalesce partial events for tool messages until a complete JSON payload is available or a configured timeout elapses; emit a "tool_message.complete" framing event with an attached schema tag. This dramatically reduces truncated tool JSON seen by SDK consumers.
- Enforce tool_choice semantics in pkg/handlers/tool_invoke_handler.go and SDKs: the compatibility layer exposes a tool_choice policy flag (first|best|ensemble). Default is "first" to match historical behavior; an explicit "best" option selects the highest-scoring tool when model outputs include scores.
- Add a JSON schema mapper pkg/codec/json_schema_mapper.go that performs lightweight validation and auto-coercion for argument types (strings->json when appropriate).
- SDK updates (python/typescript) to expose normalized ToolPayload and a small helper to rehydrate tool messages into user-friendly shapes.
- Tests: new unit and integration tests to simulate fragmented streams, variant key names, and tool_choice permutations.
- Docs: docs/openai-compat.md describing the mapping, compatibility guarantees, and migration notes.

Compatibility notes and rollout: The normalization layer is additive and default-preserving: existing apps see the same shape unless they switch the tool_choice policy. Streaming behavior is improved so consumers who previously had to tolerate partial JSON will now get complete tool messages; there is a short grace period where both old and new framing are supported (compat-shims.yaml). Linear links: ENG-2345 (compatibility mapper), ENG-2390 (streaming framer). Support ticket SUP-411 reported truncated tool JSON in production and motivated the timeout tuning.

Checklist: 
- [x] Mapper and schema coercion implemented
- [x] Streaming framer + timeout and config knobs
- [x] SDK helpers and tests
- [x] Integration tests against streaming harness
- [x] Docs and changelog updated

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Some custom consumers relied on the previous raw stream shape. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, opt-out compat shim, and clear docs with migration examples.
- Risk: Over-eager coercion could change argument types. Mitigation: mapper records coercions and we log a warning metric; coercion can be disabled per-route.

Performance: CPU impact is negligible in microbenchmarks (<1% p50 on our serving harness) due to parsing being guarded by a cheap pre-check and short-circuit for well-formed messages. Memory overhead is a few allocations per tool message.

Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2345/tool-payload-normalizer, https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2390/streaming-framer

Author(Maya): Mapper preserves unknown keys in an 'extras' map and records them for telemetry; it does not drop by default.
Priya: The streaming timeout default looks high for low-latency paths.
Author: Lowered default to 120ms for low-latency tiers and added config knob per-route; updated tests.

Author: Added docs/openai-compat.md with examples and added SDK helper functions to rehydrate legacy shapes.

release_notes: Add a compatibility normalization layer for OpenAI-style tool/function calls: canonical ToolPayload shape, streaming coalescing to avoid truncated tool JSON, configurable tool_choice policy (first|best|ensemble), SDK helpers, and docs. Default behavior preserves existing shapes; see docs/openai-compat.md for migration steps.
